event_overview.title: About Condition Hurricane Storm
event_overview.subject: Condition Hurricane Storm
event_overview.summary: Hurricane Isaias is an Atlantic tropical cyclone in the Gulf of America, tracked by the U.S. National Hurricane Center (NHC) as AL092026. It formed as Tropical Depression Nine on October 6, 2026, became Tropical Storm Isaias on October 7, and strengthened into a major hurricane while approaching the northern Gulf Coast.

facts.label: Formation and name
facts.value: The system became Tropical Depression Nine over the Gulf of America at 4:00 PM CDT on October 6, 2026, and was named Tropical Storm Isaias at 4:00 AM CDT on October 7.

facts.label: Monitoring authority
facts.value: The National Hurricane Center, part of the U.S. National Weather Service, issues the storm’s official advisories, forecasts, and U.S. coastal watch and warning products.

facts.label: Status on October 9, 2026
facts.value: At 11:00 AM CDT on October 9, Isaias had maximum sustained winds of 120 mph and a central pressure of 959 mb, placing it in Category 3—the “major hurricane” range—on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale.

facts.label: Location and movement
facts.value: At that update, the center was about 180 miles south of Pensacola, Florida, moving north-northeast at 16 mph toward the western Florida Panhandle and Alabama coast.

facts.label: Hazards and warnings
facts.value: NHC warned that the storm could bring life-threatening storm surge and destructive winds to parts of the Florida Panhandle and Alabama coast; hurricane and storm-surge warnings were in effect for portions of the northern Gulf Coast.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the October 8-9 intensification and projected Gulf Coast landfall period, not Isaias’s full development from October 6, localized warning changes, impacts, or any post-storm assessment.
